result.topic_en: Euler sets the elementary forces on the vibrating elastic lamina equal to p dx and argues that their moment about a point Y must equal the moment of elasticity K cc (ddy/dt^2), which yields the principal equation; section VIII begins computing that moment by treating Y as fixed.
result.transcription:
454 DE MOTV VIBRATORIO
quas formulam breuitatis gratia per $p\,dx$ deſigne-
mus, vt ſit vis
$YV = p\,dx = \frac{K\,dx}{2bk}\left(\frac{ddy}{dt^2}\right),$
atque has vires ita comparatas eſſe oportet, vt cum
binis illis viribus laminae in punctis A et $a$ appli-
catis in aequilibrio conſiſtant, hoc modo ſi punctum
laminae Y conſideremus, atque ambas laminae por-
tiones F Y et A Y vtrinque circa Y ſitas ſpecte-
mus, illa portio F Y nullas alias vires ſuſtinet niſi
quas hic elementares nominamus, dum altera por-
tio A Y duas inſuper vires ignotas in A et $a$ ge-
rit, quae ergo duplices vires reſpectu Y vtrinque
in aequilibrio eſſe debent, ſufficiet igitur vires por-
tioni B Y applicatas ſpectaſſe, quae quum laminae
curuaturam in ipſo puncto Y ſuſtentare debeant,
quandoquidem illis remotis portio Y F ſtatim in di-
rectum extenderetur, momentum iſtarum virium
aequari debet ipſi illi momento elaſticitatis ſupra
definito, quod erat
$= K\,cc\left(\frac{ddy}{dt^2}\right),$
vnde ſtatim principalem aequationem conſequemur,
quae totam Problematis ſolutionem continebit.

VIII. Quo igitur commodius momentum
omnium iſtarum virium elementarium reſpectu
puncti Y eruamus, hoc ipſum punctum tantiſper
quaſi fixum ſpectemus, ita vt coordinatae $x$ et $y$
pro conſtantibus habeantur, atque ab F verſus Y
progre-

items.english: the moment of these forces must equal that moment of elasticity defined above, which was = K cc (ddy/dt^2),

vnde ſtatim principalem aequationem conſequemur,

items.english: from which we shall at once obtain the principal equation, which will contain the whole solution of the Problem.

items.quote:
Quo igitur commodius momentum
omnium iſtarum virium elementarium reſpectu

items.english: So that we may more conveniently find the moment of all these elementary forces with respect to the point Y, let us for the moment regard this point as fixed, so that the coordinates x and y are taken as constants
